introduction: Today we celebrate the Baptism of the Lord, which closes the Christmas season. Isaiah announces comfort for God's people and a shepherd who carries the lambs in his arms. In the Gospel, while Jesus is praying after his baptism, the heavens open, the Spirit descends, and the Father says, You are my beloved Son. Paul tells us that God saved us through the bath of rebirth. Let us give thanks for our own Baptism.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God has saved us by the washing of rebirth and renewal in the Holy Spirit. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that all the baptized may live as beloved children of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those preparing for Baptism, and for parents bringing their children to the font: that they may receive this gift with faith. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who need comfort: that the Lord may carry them like a shepherd carries his lambs. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have forgotten their Baptism or left the faith: that they may hear God's voice calling them his beloved again. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may live soberly, justly and devoutly as we wait for the blessed hope of Christ's coming. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty God, at the Jordan you proclaimed Jesus your beloved Son and anointed him with the Holy Spirit. Keep us, your children born of water and the Spirit, faithful to our calling. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: You are my beloved Son
reflection.body:
Isaiah's words open with tenderness: "Comfort, comfort my people," says your God. A voice cries out to prepare a highway in the desert, and the prophet describes the God who is coming: "He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom."

In Luke's Gospel, the people wonder whether John might be the Messiah. John points beyond himself: "he comes who is mightier than I." Then Luke tells of Jesus' baptism in a few words, and he adds a detail of his own: Jesus "had been baptized and was praying." Luke loves to show Jesus at prayer at the great moments of his life.

While he prays, "The sky was opened, and the Holy Spirit descended in a bodily form like a dove on him." And the Father speaks: "You are my beloved Son. In you I am well pleased." Jesus begins his mission knowing who he is and how much he is loved.

The Letter to Titus tells us what Baptism means for us: "not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit." In our Baptism, the Father says to each of us what he said to Jesus: you are my beloved child.

This feast is a good day to remember our own Baptism. Find out the date if you do not know it, and celebrate it like a birthday. When you bless yourself with holy water at the church door, remember that you are a beloved child of God. And pray, as Jesus did, before every important step.
